rows.question: Which VR/AR headsets and XR hardware has he worked with?
rows.answer:
Washington has worked with several VR/AR headsets and XR hardware:

- [redacted 2026-10-18: outdated claim]
- **RayNeo Air 4 Pro glasses:** he is developing a heads-up display for these AR glasses [2].
- **HTC Vive:** used in the VR Runner maze game and the DJI Matrice 600 Pro VR simulator [2].
- **Leap Motion:** used in the DJI simulator and in hardware integration at Inmersoft [2][3].
- **HoloLens:** mentioned in AR heads-up display work for Inmersoft [6].
- **Other hardware:** Emotiv EEG, haptics, Arduino and IoT devices in Inmersoft projects [3], plus muscle and heart-rate sensors in VR Runner [2].

rows.question: Tell me about the synchronized multi-headset VR experience he built for a corporate wellness session.
rows.answer: [redacted 2026-10-18: outdated claim] The session opened with an 11-minute 8K 360° guided meditation with spatial audio (Meta XR Audio SDK), followed by a head-movement rhythm game, and it was designed for first-time VR users at a corporate wellness session [2]. The project was delivered through his studio, Inmersoft, which he founded in 2018 [1].

rows.question: What did he work on at Sansar?
rows.answer: At Sansar (Linden Lab), Washington worked as a Game Developer on a contract through BairesDev, remote, in 2022 [1][2]. He built avatar interaction mechanics and a dynamic animation system for a social VR platform [2]. He also optimized shaders and materials, reducing memory usage by about 40% [1][2][4]. According to his LinkedIn profile, the contract ran from July to November 2022 and included testing new spatial audio features [4].

rows.question: What is SkyNest?
rows.answer: SkyNest is a multiplayer VR combat sandbox that Washington is developing, currently in development [1]. Its described features include physics-based hands, melee and ranged weapons, armor with durability and grenades, and PvP duels on a self-hosted game server [1]. It is built with Unity 6, Meta Quest, Netcode for GameObjects, and Laravel + React, with a passwordless account flow inside VR and an admin panel and backend deployed to a VPS with GitHub Actions [1].

rows.question: What AR work did he do for Merge?
rows.answer: Washington worked for Merge as an Augmented Reality Consultant on a contract from April to July 2020, remotely, for an AR educational content company (Merge Cube). He researched moving Merge Cube tracking from Vuforia to native Unity AR Foundation and built 3 cube-detection prototypes with ARKit and ARCore [1]. His CV describes the same role as AR Research Engineer, where he led the migration research from Vuforia to Unity AR Foundation, unifying ARKit/ARCore object recognition and validating cross-platform 3D detection [2][3].

rows.question: Production ML experience
rows.answer: Washington has taken ML models into production, most notably on the Buscapez platform. He built a 4-class YOLO detector in PyTorch (mAP50 0.96) and exported it to ONNX for the server and to ExecuTorch for offline inference on iOS and Android [4]. He deployed a FastAPI + ONNX Runtime inference service that runs at 49 ms per image and 70 MB of RAM on a 2-core VPS shared with other systems [4]. [redacted 2026-10-18: outdated claim, see PROJECT.md P20c] He also shipped a human-in-the-loop data pipeline with assisted annotation, hash-based deduplication and YOLO export for incremental retraining [4]. [redacted 2026-10-18: outdated claim, see PROJECT.md P20c]

rows.question: What mAP did his YOLO detector reach?
rows.answer: Washington's YOLO detector for the Buscapez species-identification module reached a mAP50 of 0.96 on validation [1][2][3]. [redacted 2026-10-18: outdated claim, see PROJECT.md P20c]

rows.question: How did he fix the accuracy problem of the on-device model in the mobile app?
rows.answer: [redacted 2026-10-18: outdated claim, see PROJECT.md P20c] In the CV version, this is described as diagnosing the input distortion in the mobile runtime, with the same accuracy gain [3].

rows.question: Does he have experience serving LLMs locally on his own hardware?
rows.answer: Yes. Washington runs a self-hosted llama.cpp server running Gemma (26B QAT) at 130–175 tokens/s on an RTX 4090, with tool calling, shared across the local network [1]. His skills list includes local LLM serving with llama.cpp [3][5].

rows.question: What did he build with LLMs at Laboratorios Bagó?
rows.answer: [redacted 2026-10-18: outdated claim] The tool was used at the company's MKT Attack creative event [1][2]. His listed skills include Large Language Models (LLM) and the Claude API [2].

rows.question: Has he published research on VR rehabilitation using haptic devices?
rows.answer:
Yes. Washington has published several papers on VR rehabilitation using haptic devices:

- A 2018 paper on a haptic stimulation glove for fine motor rehabilitation in VR, which uses flexibility sensors and vibratory actuators to give feedback on contact with virtual surfaces [1].
- A 2016 paper on upper limb rehabilitation with force feedback, using the Novint Falcon haptic device together with Oculus Rift and Leap Motion [2].

He also worked on VR therapy for children with cerebral palsy and on bilateral teleoperation with haptic feedback during his time at ARSI Research Lab [4].

rows.question: Does he hold any registered software intellectual property?
rows.answer: Yes. Washington holds a registered software IP: the Virtual 2D Laser Sensor, registered with the Ecuadorian Intellectual Property Institute under QUI-052058 in 2017 [1]. It is described as a C# LIDAR simulation connected to MATLAB [6].

rows.question: Which of his papers compared WebGL and WebVR performance?
rows.answer:
Two of his papers compared WebGL and WebVR performance:

- "Performance evaluation of WebGL and WebVR apps in VR environments" (ISVC, Springer LNCS, 2019). It measured device and browser performance, finding WebGL and WebVR similar on PC, while WebVR performed notably better than WebGL on mobile devices [1].
- "Performance of WebGL standard for displaying 3D applications on mobile devices" (CISTI, IEEE, 2021). It analyzed WebGL performance on mobile, finding that compression formats, connection speeds and browsers affect loading times, performance and build size [2].

rows.question: What is My Style AR?
rows.answer: My Style AR is an augmented reality application proposed in a 2018 paper. It lets users preview furniture in real time before buying, and modify size, color and texture, with relevant product information shown as they interact [2]. The app includes a catalog of living room, dining room and bedroom furniture and is designed for handheld devices that support augmented reality level 2.0 [2]. The paper was published at the International Conference on Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality and Computer Graphics (AVR, Springer LNCS) [2].

rows.question: Has he done any work on eye tracking or gaze estimation?
rows.answer:
Yes. Washington published a paper on a non-invasive eye-tracking system that uses a Tobii Eye Tracking sensor to evaluate students during reading or visual appreciation tasks [1].

He also built Gazetrack, a webcam-based gaze tracking project. It uses MediaPipe Face Mesh for head pose and a ResNet-18 gaze model running on CUDA to estimate gaze direction, then maps gaze to screen coordinates with a calibrated polynomial regression and a One-Euro smoothing filter [2][4]. The project also includes a 5x5 held-out accuracy evaluation and an optional local activity logger [2].

rows.question: What is Plan Vivo?
rows.answer:
Plan Vivo is a project plan kept in one JSON file, which AI coding agents keep up to date, along with a local live viewer that shows phases, real time spent per actor, and a calibrated projection of when the work will finish [2]. The plan is split into phases containing items of three kinds: `prompt` (a task for the agent), `gate` (a human approval) and `unplanned` (something that came up along the way) [1].

The kit includes commands for validating plans, rebuilding time segments from Claude Code session logs and git history, and migrating older plan formats [1][4]. The viewer is a localhost React app that reloads whenever `plan.json` is saved and supports Spanish and English [1].

Washington built this project and has described its key design decisions, such as deriving computed values in the viewer instead of storing them, measuring time from logs rather than asking agents to report it, and using a single install with versioned data [6].

rows.question: How does the Localia platform make sure GPU worker results are not lost?
rows.answer: The sources say Localia uses Redis for worker results and tackled a message-loss problem. The worker pushes results to a Redis list, and the listener consumes them using `BLMOVE` into a processing list. A message is removed only after it has been handled, leftover messages are recovered on restart, and TCP keepalive is enabled to detect dead connections [3][2]. Earlier attempts with pub/sub and `BLPOP` were dropping messages if the listener lost its connection right after the pop [3]. The listener runs as a long-running, supervised Artisan command [2][4]. Result delivery is described as guaranteed [5].

rows.question: Tell me about his forex trading system project.
rows.answer:
Washington built a forex trading system: a platform for designing, backtesting, validating and running algorithmic forex strategies on MetaTrader 5, combining a Laravel + React web app with a Python FastAPI bridge to the MT5 terminal [1]. It is a personal research project, and the sources state it is not financial advice and does not claim any strategy is profitable [1].

Key features include:
- 15 parameterised strategy types, with an event-driven pandas backtester and a parallel Strategy Explorer that ranks results on out-of-sample data [2][5].
- A market regime classifier, a historical bot, and AI analysis of backtest results [2].
- A live bot for demo accounts, with daily loss limits, circuit breakers, a portfolio heat limit and a news filter [4].
- Operations tooling such as Telegram alerts, a Windows watchdog and a desktop control panel [3][4].

He split the system along the platform constraint: the MT5 Python library runs only on Windows, so it sits in a localhost-bound bridge protected by an API key [3][5].

rows.question: How many agent states does the Agent Office Visualizer engine track, and what project is it based on?
rows.answer: The state engine tracks 21 states, as described in its catalog of states [2][4]. The project extends claude-office by Paul Robello and contributors, released under the MIT license, and its first 232 commits are that upstream history [1].

rows.question: What accuracy does his webcam gaze tracker achieve?
rows.answer:
The sources describe how the gaze tracker measures accuracy, but they do not report a final accuracy figure. The project evaluates accuracy on a held-out 5x5 grid and reports error by zone (center, edges, corners) and in a 3x3 regional breakdown, in px, % of screen width, cm and degrees [1]. It is run with the `evaluate` command [4]. No specific error values are given in the sources.

The sources also note that the project measures accuracy against a dedicated eye tracker's infrared hardware: it tests how much accuracy a 1080p webcam can reach [1]. The exact numbers are not stated, so for the results themselves, see his LinkedIn profile: https://www.linkedin.com/in/wxquevedo

rows.question: Which company did he found and when?
rows.answer: Washington founded Inmersoft, an engineering company based in Quito, in September 2018 [3]. He describes it as his own company, where he serves as Founder & Principal Engineer, and it has delivered 200+ projects since then [3][5].

rows.question: What is his role with Stanford University?
rows.answer: Washington works as a Software & AI Consultant for Stanford University, contracted through Inmersoft, an official Stanford supplier, on a remote basis since July 2026 [1][3]. His work centers on the Buscapez project, a tuna-tagging research platform, where he built the species-identification module [2][3].

rows.question: What did he build at Arlift?
rows.answer: At Arlift, Washington worked as a Platform Engineer on a contract basis, starting in October 2025 [1][2]. He built a QHSE compliance platform for an oil and gas operator, with a Laravel API and a React SPA [1][2]. The platform includes RBAC, a workflow engine, audit logging, an org chart built with React Flow, geospatial maps built with Leaflet, and 5 compliance modules [1][2]. It is covered by 308 automated tests [1][2].

rows.question: What did he do at WebCreek?
rows.answer: At WebCreek he worked as a Unity 3D Developer on a contract from November 2019 to March 2020 [1][2]. The project was TrainBeyond, an Omni VR training product, where he built character animation driven by real-time motion capture and visual effects for in-game actions [1].

rows.question: ¿Qué es vSpace y cuántos usuarios tiene?
rows.answer: vSpace es la plataforma de visitas médicas usada por la fuerza de ventas de Laboratorios Bagó del Ecuador. Incluye literatura, registro de visitas, promociones y aplicaciones interactivas, además de 20 minijuegos integrados [2][3]. Washington la desarrolló como parte de su trabajo en la empresa [1][2]. La plataforma tiene 400 usuarios y registra 20.000 interacciones mensuales [1][2][3].

rows.question: ¿Qué premios o reconocimientos ha recibido?
rows.answer:
Washington ha recibido los siguientes premios y reconocimientos:

- **Best Young Researcher Award**, Universidad de las Fuerzas Armadas ESPE, junio de 2017 [1].
- **Primer lugar, Galardones Nacionales SENESCYT**, categoría Educación, Ecuador, noviembre de 2016 [1].
- **Ganador del Movistar Challenge** en Campus Party Quito 4, Movistar Ecuador, septiembre de 2014 (categoría Smart App, EduCanal) [1].

rows.question: ¿Qué tecnologías usa su aplicación sobre la hipótesis de Riemann?
rows.answer: La aplicación es una web estática hecha con React y TypeScript, y se construye con Vite [1][2]. Los cálculos matemáticos se implementan en TypeScript, y los gráficos usan Plotly para las líneas, un shader GLSL en WebGL para la coloración de dominio y Canvas2D para la animación de la fórmula explícita [3]. Las fórmulas se muestran con KaTeX y la navegación usa React Router [3][4]. Los ceros de la función zeta se precalculan offline con Python y mpmath a 30 cifras decimales [5].
